intro: Kimi Antonelli became F1's world champion at just 20 years old, and the Milwaukee Brewers finally broke through with their first-ever World Series title behind MVP William Contreras — it's been a wild week in sports. Oh, and Lamar Jackson's thumb is suddenly Baltimore's biggest problem.

stories.headline: Lamar Jackson's Thumb Could Sink Baltimore's Season
stories.body: The Ravens' MVP quarterback is heading to surgery and IR after a thumb injury, meaning Baltimore loses him for at least four games at the worst possible time. A team built around one guy just found out what life looks like without him.

stories.headline: Bears Go All-In, Trade Two First-Rounders for Jeffery Simmons
stories.body: Chicago ripped a premium defensive tackle away from Tennessee at the deadline, paying two first-round picks plus more to land the All-Pro Simmons. The Bears are done being cute about rebuilding — they want in now.

stories.headline: Washington Stomps Philly 27–10 as Eagles' Collapse Hits Six Straight Losses
stories.body: The Commanders handed Philadelphia its sixth consecutive defeat, dropping the Eagles to 2–6 and pushing them to the edge of NFC East irrelevance. Washington is 2–4–1 and somehow the healthier-looking franchise in this rivalry right now.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli, Age 20, Is Your New F1 World Champion
stories.body: Antonelli finished third in Mexico City on Sunday to clinch the 2026 Drivers' Championship with four races still to go, becoming the youngest world champion in F1 history. The kid replaced Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes and immediately won the title — no pressure or anything.

stories.headline: Verstappen Wins in Mexico, Nudges Hamilton Out of Second by Two Points
stories.body: Max Verstappen took his third win of the season in Mexico City, with Hamilton crossing the line second for Ferrari — a result that still wasn't enough to hold off Verstappen in the standings, 261 to 259. With Antonelli already 119 points clear, those two are essentially racing each other for the runner-up trophy.

stories.headline: Mercedes Nearly Clinched Everything in Mexico — Nearly
stories.body: Antonelli's title sealed one half of a potential historic double for Mercedes, but the constructors' championship slipped through their fingers for now, with Ferrari and Red Bull keeping the gap alive. São Paulo is next, and Mercedes — sitting 126 points clear — will get another shot.

stories.headline: Milwaukee Finally Does It: Brewers Win First World Series, Contreras Named MVP
stories.body: The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history, with catcher Willson Contreras taking home MVP honors. Rookie Cooper Pratt broke a 48-year-old World Series record, Sal Frelick did the Lambeau Leap, and manager Pat Murphy took a shot at the Yankees — so basically a perfect week in Wisconsin.

stories.headline: Skubal Sweepstakes Are On: Dodgers, Mets and Cubs All Want the Same Guy
stories.body: Tarik Skubal is the hottest name in the early offseason, with the Dodgers, Mets, and Cubs all circling before the December 1 lockout deadline. Three of the richest teams in baseball chasing one pitcher — this should go smoothly.

stories.headline: Options Chaos: Royals Cut Estévez, Cardinals Drop Stanek, Padres Pass on Canning and Giolito
stories.body: The offseason roster shuffle is already underway, with Kansas City declining Carlos Estévez's $13 million option, St. Louis cutting Ryne Stanek loose, and San Diego passing on both Griffin Canning and Lucas Giolito. The Brewers are also open to trading closer Trevor Megill, so the relief pitcher market is about to get very crowded.

stories.headline: The NBA Is Basically a MASH Unit Right Now
stories.body: Nine All-Stars — including Anthony Edwards (two months, knee), Chet Holmgren (8-10 weeks, patellar tendon), and Jalen Williams (fractured fibula, season TBD) — are already sidelined with multiweek injuries before November even starts. It's the worst early-season injury wave in recent memory, and your fantasy team is cooked.

stories.headline: Curry Is Ageless and This Warriors Rookie Just Scored 37
stories.body: Stephen Curry dropped 99 points across three games — including a perfect 8-for-8 night in Denver — to fuel a four-game Warriors winning streak, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg piled on with 37 points against the Clippers, the most by a Golden State rookie since Curry himself scored 42 back in 2010. Golden State is quietly having a good time while the rest of the league is in a walking boot.

stories.headline: Porzingis on the Block as Warriors Eye a Trade
stories.body: Golden State is shopping Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely while dealing with a private health issue that has him questioning his basketball future. Meanwhile, the broader trade market is buzzing around names like Norman Powell and Lauri Markkanen — though Markkanen already has his own problems, listed day-to-day with a wrist sprain.

stories.headline: Kucherov Wants Out of Tampa and the Lightning Are Playing Dumb
stories.body: Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign an extension and wants a trade, but Tampa Bay is publicly insisting he's going nowhere. At $9.5 million with a 10-team no-trade list and UFA status looming, this standoff has all the makings of a very awkward road trip.

stories.headline: Dylan Larkin Has Left the Building — Literally
stories.body: Larkin didn't just request a trade from Detroit, he walked out and is now suspended without pay while the Red Wings wait for an offer they actually like. Montreal is being floated as a destination, which would be quite the consolation prize for a franchise that's been rebuilding since roughly the Obama administration.

stories.headline: Seattle Flips Shane Wright to Nashville in a Bet-on-the-Future Swap
stories.body: The Kraken traded 2022 fourth-overall pick Shane Wright to the Predators for 6-foot-4 winger Matthew Wood, a first-rounder from 2023 — a straight one-for-one before either player hits restricted free agency this summer. Both teams are essentially trading question marks and hoping theirs turns into an answer.

stories.headline: USC Embarrasses Ohio State, Sends Buckeyes Tumbling Out of the Top 10
stories.body: The Trojans dismantled No. 2 Ohio State 24–7, with Trent Mosley setting the tone on a 69-yard touchdown grab while the Buckeyes played without injured QB Julian Sayin. Rough week to be in Columbus.

stories.headline: Florida State Fires Mike Norvell With a $50 Million Send-Off
stories.body: After three straight losses, the Seminoles showed Norvell the door — and handed him what's reportedly one of the largest buyouts in college football history. At least someone's winning in Tallahassee.

stories.headline: Indiana Stays Perfect at 8–0, Survives Minnesota in Overtime Thriller
stories.body: The Hoosiers escaped Minneapolis 23–16 in OT, courtesy of a 60-yard field goal and a game-winning play to open the extra period. Indiana is quietly becoming the most interesting undefeated team in the country.

stories.headline: Zverev Reaches the Summit: First German World No. 1 Since Becker
stories.body: Alexander Zverev claimed the ATP's top ranking on Monday, bumping Jannik Sinner to No. 2 after a season that included Roland Garros and US Open titles. Germany hadn't had a men's No. 1 since Boris Becker in 1991, so no pressure or anything.

stories.headline: Alcaraz Steamrolls Vienna, Wawrinka Quietly Calls It a Career
stories.body: Carlos Alcaraz dismantled Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in just 87 minutes to win the Vienna Open and stay perfect in ATP 500 finals this season. Meanwhile in Basel, Stan Wawrinka lost to Jiri Lehecka and walked off the court for the last time, closing a career that included three Grand Slam titles.

stories.headline: Dart Breaks Through, Vacherot Makes Monaco History
stories.body: Harriet Dart won her first WTA title at the Guangzhou Open, while Valentin Vacherot took the Basel ATP 500 crown to become the first Monegasque player ever to win at that level. A solid week for first-timers.

stories.headline: Andrew Novak Goes Wire-to-Wire in Mexico, Wins by Five
stories.body: Andrew Novak claimed his first PGA Tour title at the VidantaWorld Mexico Open, closing with a 69 to finish at 25-under and beat Steven Fisk and Kristoffer Ventura by five strokes. He built a six-shot cushion through the middle rounds and never looked back — a pretty comfortable way to get your first win.

stories.headline: LIV's Exodus Continues: Oosthuizen and Poulter Both Head for the Door
stories.body: Louis Oosthuizen is joining Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, and David Puig in leaving LIV Golf for the DP World Tour, while Ian Poulter has also quit LIV and insists his playing days aren't done. At this rate, LIV's roster is going to need a serious restock.

stories.headline: Chacarra Tops Race to Dubai After India Win, Playoff Season Underway
stories.body: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship at 21-under to jump to the top of the Race to Dubai standings, ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy with three events left. The Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship has also kicked off the tour's playoff run, with Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton making their first starts since ditching LIV Golf 2.0.

stories.headline: Kane Finally Gets His Flowers: England's Striker Wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or
stories.body: Harry Kane took home the 2026 Ballon d'Or after a ridiculous 61-goal, 51-game season for Bayern Munich — a number that sounds made up but isn't. Alexia Putellas claimed the women's award, because Barcelona apparently just has those lying around.

stories.headline: Pepi's Back and PSV Did Not Take It Easy on Willem II
stories.body: Ricardo Pepi returned from injury and immediately contributed a goal and an assist in PSV's 7–0 demolition of Willem II on October 31. Nothing like easing back into match fitness by being part of a scoreline that should come with an apology.

stories.headline: Nico Williams Isn't Going Anywhere — He Told Arsenal, Barca, and Everyone Else Thanks But No
stories.body: Nico Williams shut down interest from Arsenal, Barcelona, and a handful of other European clubs by signing a new long-term deal with Athletic Club through 2035. Loyalty is rare in modern football, and apparently so is the bag Athletic Club must have offered.
